module


public import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Basic
public import Mathlib.Data.Fin.Basic

@[expose] public section

/-!
# Property B

A family of sets has *property B* when the ground set admits a 2-colouring under which no member
of the family is monochromatic. For 3-uniform hypergraphs this is
`ThreeUniformHypergraph.IsTwoColorable`.
-/

namespace Finset

/-- A family `F` of finite sets has **property B** (equivalently, chromatic number `2`) if there
is a `2`-colouring of the ground set under which no member of `F` is monochromatic. -/
def HasPropertyB {α : Type*} (F : Finset (Finset α)) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : α → Fin 2, ∀ A ∈ F, ∃ x ∈ A, ∃ y ∈ A, f x ≠ f y

end Finset

findings.description: The parenthetical “equivalently, chromatic number `2`” at line 34 is inaccurate for the empty family, which the definition permits. `(∅ : Finset (Finset α)).HasPropertyB` holds for every ground type, whereas an edgeless hypergraph has chromatic number 0 on an empty ground set and 1 on a nonempty ground set. The definition correctly expresses two-colourability, or chromatic number at most 2; only this parenthetical is wrong. The empty cases and agreement with Mathlib graph two-colourability were verified in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Property_B, identifies Property B with 2-colourability. Wood, “Hypergraph Colouring and Degeneracy,” arXiv:1310.2972, Introduction footnote, defines chromatic number as the minimum number of colours in a proper colouring. Mathlib's Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Coloring/Vertex.lean explicitly defines `Colorable n` using “at most n colors” and proves `chromaticNumber_bot = 1` for a nonempty vertex type and chromatic number 0 for an empty vertex type.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “(equivalently, chromatic number `2`)” with “(equivalently, chromatic number at most `2`)”. Alternatively, qualify the exact-equality claim by requiring the family to be nonempty. Leave the definition unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The classical definition uses a set B that meets every family member but contains none of them. Lean instead uses a single colouring `α → Fin 2` and two differently coloured witnesses in each member, with no finiteness assumption on the ambient type.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Given the colouring, take B to be its colour-0 class. Two unequal values in Fin 2 necessarily include both colours, so each edge meets B and its complement. Conversely, the indicator colouring of such a B supplies the required witnesses. Because the family and its members are finite, B can be restricted to the finite union of the members; allowing an arbitrary ambient type changes nothing. These equivalences were proved in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`, including a finite splitting-set characterization. The same file proves agreement with Mathlib's graph `Colorable 2`; agreement with `ThreeUniformHypergraph.ofFinset(...).IsTwoColorable` is definitional.

review.notes: No mathematical definition or use-site mismatch was found. The sole actual user is `Erdos1022.SparseImpliesPropertyB`; the similarly named definition in Erdős 602 is independent. Both scratch files compiled without errors or warnings, and the proved equivalences use no sorry axioms. Tests covered empty ground types and families, empty and singleton edges, the one-edge cardinality threshold, triangles, and the Fano plane. Use-site checks covered parameter monotonicity and zero/nonpositive boundary values. The live 1022 page has an affirmative status banner inconsistent with its own negative-answer text; its substantive text and Wood's construction support the file's recorded negative solution, so no status change is recommended. The full Lo68 paper was not retrieved; the source itself says that paper does not contain the attributed result. The reviewed file remains byte-for-byte identical to the committed version; pre-existing sandbox configuration changes were left untouched.
